clue.text: On receiving a pardon, go and eat a lot

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: a go, or turn, at eating to excess

indicators.note: receiving here means the first word takes the next piece straight after it

parts.note: on in the sense of above or atop can be over
an indulgence was a church pardon remitting punishment for sin

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates being let off by heading out for a huge meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' is a noun in the definition, a turn at eating too much, so the whole phrase stands for the noun answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess in food or drink is exactly what a bout of eating far too much amounts to.

clue.text: He changes but doesn't start to go round!

indicators.note: doesn't start tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for something that turns

parts.note: something that goes round, like a turning drum, is a revolver

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a man who keeps altering but refuses to turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' drops the first letter, R, from REVOLVER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gradually develops into new forms is someone who changes over time.

clue.text: That means about 550 are not working

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the two letters of the abbreviation go round the numerals

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is
in Roman numerals D is 500 and L is 50

explanation.surface: Someone works out that some 550 staff are off the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Unemployed or inactive people are described as doing nothing, the plain sense of idle.

clue.text: Made off when temporary accommodation was put into action

indicators.note: put into means one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a camp is tents or huts for a short stay

explanation.surface: People fled when tents were pitched as part of a military operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away or leave suddenly is to have bolted, a synonym.

clue.text: Polishing might result in a shine

indicators.note: polishing suggests working over and reshaping the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Rubbing at something may give it a gleam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polishing' seems to belong to the shine but it rearranges RESULT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam or sheen on a surface is a synonym for a shine.

clue.text: Measure the window for packing in a crate

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
a casement is a hinged window

explanation.surface: Instructions to size up a window before boxing it for shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosing something in a box or case is the act of packing it up.

clue.text: In the middle of the action the French came right back after American money

indicators.note: after places the reversed pieces behind the coin

parts.note: a cent is a US coin

indicators.note: came back tells us the two following pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: A tale of action in which the French returned after a dollar payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LA plus R into RAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the centre or core of something means being in its middle.

clue.text: Excitation leads to a bad end when too much alcohol flows

indicators.note: flows suggests the letters run freely into a new order
end picks out the final letter of the word bad

explanation.surface: Agitation can come to a nasty finish when the drink is flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' takes D, the final letter of 'bad', and 'flows' shuffles it with EXCITATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunkenness is the state of a person after taking far more drink than is wise.

clue.text: Gathers people for prayers…

explanation.surface: Someone rounds up a congregation for worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble people is to bring them together; in church a short set prayer for a given day has the same name.

clue.text: … led by this chap making a noise

definitions.text: … led by this chap making a noise

parts.words: … led by this chap making a noise
parts.note: following on from the prayers, a cathedral clergyman leads them, and a near-identical sounding gun makes a bang

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: worship led by a man raising his voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral clergyman leads prayers, and his title sounds like a big gun that booms.

clue.text: Noticed that a man was making the pudding

parts.note: spotted means noticed or seen
Dick is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone saw that a fellow was cooking dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOTTED DICK is a British steamed suet pudding studded with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British dessert of suet sponge and dried fruit, a kind of pudding.

clue.text: Provide a footpath for quiet residential street

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
Ave is short for avenue, a tree-lined street

explanation.surface: A council plans a pavement for a peaceful suburban road.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay a hard surface for walkers is to surface a path with slabs.

clue.text: Organiser of the entertainment I saw in Paris and Rome

indicators.note: saw is taken as cutting up, so the letters are cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller saw shows in two European capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of see but is the anagram signal, as if sawing the letters apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical producer or promoter arranges shows and concerts.

clue.text: Instrument about which young lady came back very quietly

annotationWithheld.why: Instrument about which young lady came back very quietly (10): PIANO round reversed MISS gives only nine letters; the second I of PIANISSIMO has no source, and no clue word supplies it
annotationWithheld.clue: Instrument about which young lady came back very quietly

clue.text: Name some sort of site for industrious builders

parts.note: a term is a word or name for something

indicators.note: some sort of suggests a reshaped version of the next word

explanation.surface: Asking for the name of a kind of building site.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects construct huge mounds, so they are tireless builders.

clue.text: If Buddhist leader returns he will arrive at Italian resort

indicators.note: returns means the words before are read backwards

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist teacher

explanation.surface: A Buddhist teacher's homecoming, should it happen, would land him in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns IF plus LAMA into AMALFI.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on Italy's Campanian coast is a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Being more of a glutton, some agreed, I erred

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An admission that a group conceded someone was wrong about appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a bigger appetite for food is the hungrier, the comparative of a glutton's trait.

clue.text: Fur which I hesitate to say belongs to me

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
mine means belonging to me

explanation.surface: Someone shyly admits a fur coat is theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: The white winter coat of the stoat is a prized pelt.

clue.text: Tennis player gave many an annoying encore!

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many

indicators.note: annoying suggests the word encore is disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A star gave lots of irritating extra performances.
explanation.walkthrough: John McEnroe was an American tennis champion famous for his tantrums.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous American tennis champion of the 1980s.

clue.text: Girl employed to cut everything back

parts.note: to prune is to cut back

indicators.note: back means the word for everything is read in reverse

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A girl hired to trim the entire garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Ill after the circuit I made on tiny bits of lava

indicators.note: after puts the word for sick behind the circuit

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: Someone felt sick after running laps over volcanic grit.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fragments thrown out by volcanoes are a geological term for ejected particles.

clue.text: Competent, in a perverse way, at making charts

indicators.note: in places the word for competent inside the turned letters
perverse means turned the wrong way, so the street abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: St is street, a way
able means competent

explanation.surface: Someone skilled, though contrary, at drawing graphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverse' turns ST into TS, and 'in' puts ABLE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lists of data in rows and columns are a kind of chart.

clue.text: Firmly established in chairs a long way down

parts.note: deep means far below
seated means sitting in chairs

explanation.surface: People sitting far below in an amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rooted and entrenched is firmly fixed, a synonym.

clue.text: Peas squashed into a recess

indicators.note: squashed suggests the letters of peas are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Peas pressed into a nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Say thank you to Elsie for the powder

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: say signals that the name is taken as spoken

parts.note: the name sounds like the two letters L and C

explanation.surface: Someone thanks Elsie for some talcum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' tells you to hear 'Elsie' as L-C.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft mineral ground fine, used as a dusting powder.

clue.text: Some of the decor Gilda chose for the dog

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Gilda picked part of the décor for her pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'chose for the dog' as definition; 'chose for' is the surface verb and link, so only 'the dog' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged Welsh herding breed, an example of a dog.

clue.text: Lacy one all made by the ordinary folk

indicators.note: made suggests the letters are made into something new

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Lace items all produced by ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by laypeople rather than clergy, in the manner of non-clerics.

clue.text: Changing the form by cutting corners

definitions.text: Changing the form by cutting corners

indicators.note: changing tells us to alter the order of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Reshaping something by trimming its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines rebuilding into a new shape, and also rearranges CUTTING CORNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebuilding something into a new shape is changing its form.
